name: The Kalakaua Park Banyan
transport: No dedicated stop; central downtown Hilo, an easy walk from the bayfront and most Hilo accommodation
verify_notes: One of two banyans planted by Sheriff and later Postmaster Luther Severance in 1882 at the west end of the park (Wikipedia; mycityhunt.com, both independently give the same account). The other original tree was relocated about 5 miles to Kaumana by Sheriff George Williams when Waianuenue Ave was widened. A 1964 newspaper account instead credited King Kalakaua himself with the planting; the two accounts disagree and neither source resolves it, delivered as a flag rather than a pick. The tree survived at least one attempt to cut it down after it damaged a water main, and was deliberately retained during the park's 1933-34 redesign by landscape architects Robert O. and Catherine Thompson, who reportedly seated the King Kalakaua statue rather than standing it partly so it would not be overshadowed by the canopy. Register (Hawaii Exceptional Trees #1170) gives 18.6m girth and 78ft height, vitality Good; this girth is a banyan's buttressed aerial-root mass, not a single trunk, and must never be presented as a trunk measurement or used to derive an age via growth rate. Age instead comes from the documented 1882 planting: about 144 years as of 2026. Register coordinate is park-level (19.7300,-155.0900), shared with the Divi-Divi and Loulu Palm register entries also in this park; Wikipedia narrows it to 'the west end of the park' but that is still not a tree-level pin.
